reductionFrom.formalDefinition: Partition = <S, I> | S is a set of positive integers and there exists a subset of S, I where the sum of I's elements equals the sum of elements not in set I
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: The partition problem is the task of deciding whether a given multiset S of positive integers can be partitioned into two subsets S1 and S2 such that the sum of the numbers in S1 equals the sum of the numbers in S2
reductionFrom.inputDescription: S, a multiset of positive integers
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether S can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Format: {N | N subset int} (a set of positive integers S; duplicate values in the input collapse to one) Example: {1,7,12,15,33,12,11,5,6,9,21,18}
reductionFrom.certificateFormat: Format: (S1),(S2) | S1,S2 partition S exactly (each element used once), sum(S1) = sum(S2) Example: (33,21,15),(1,7,12,11,5,6,9,18)

reductionTo.formalDefinition: Weighted Cut = {<G, k> | G is a graph with cut of size k}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: A weighted cut in an undirected graph is a partition of the graph's vertices into two complementary sets S and T, and the size of the cut is the sum of edge weights between S and T.
reductionTo.inputDescription: G, a weighted graph, and k, a target cut weight
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether the given edge subset forms a cut of total weight exactly k
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.instanceFormat: Format: {((N,E),K) | N is set, E subset {(e, w) | e is N unorderedcross N, w is int}, K is int} Example: (({1,2,3,4,5},{({2,1},5),({1,3},4),({2,3},2),({3,5},1),({2,4},4),({4,5},2)}),5) Parallel edges: when two edges join the same nodes, their weights are added, and a certificate lists the pair once with the total. An edge written twice with the same weight, either way round, counts once.
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Format: {S | S subset E, sum of edge weights in S = K} Example: {({2,1},5)}
